chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the wealth of the orphan, he said: The worker with it is liable (guarantor), and for the orphan is the profit when there is no wealth for the worker with it. And he said: If it incurs loss, he pays it.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial liability of an agent managing an orphan's wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'daman' (guarantee) for agents managing orphan wealth, emphasizing that profit accrues to the orphan while the agent bears the risk of loss, particularly when acting without co-investment. Scholarly tradition interprets this as a protective measure to prevent negligence, ensuring that the guardian's personal capital is not merely a formality but a genuine stake in the venture's success. This ruling underscores the fiduciary duty's strictness in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the orphan's financial security over the agent's convenience.
